newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: Bolivian MRTA member accused of kidnapping.
newsitem.headline: Bolivian MRTA member accused of kidnapping.

text.p: A Bolivian member of the rebel group that held hostages at the Japanese ambassador's home in Peru for four months was charged on Monday with the 1995 kidnapping of a Bolivia businessman.
Hugo Pedro Avellaneda, a member of Peru's Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA), was among those charged with the 1995 kidnapping of Bolivian businessman Samuel Doria Medina, court sources said.
The court also listed Nestor Cerpa, the head of the MRTA group that stormed the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima, as one of those involved in the 1995 kidnapping.
Cerpa and 13 other guerrillas were killed when Peruvian commandos stormed the Japanese ambassador's residence and freed 71 of 72 hostages. One hostage and two commandos also died in the assault.
The 45-day kidnapping of Medina led to the payment of a $1.2 million ransom. That money was used to finance the December attack on the Japanese residence, according to local press reports.
